title: Extract run clock and delayed work; share searchable Workshop choices
context: Continue the architecture-first foundation while improving the long, difficult-to-navigate lab dropdowns. Visual labs use lil-gui and sound/units also have native controls.
outcome: The pure run context owns motion time, restart generation and stale-callback guards. A platform timer adapter cancels hack endings, destruction previews and death holds on restart and disposal, preserving the original advance/reset sites. A Workshop-only host enhances selects with eight or more options through one searchable modal, retaining existing value/change/preset paths. It supports keyboard navigation, explicit Escape close, current selection, disabled options, dynamic controls and observer cleanup. Commands/events, random streams, full renderer disposal, broader panel organization and missile integration remain pending.
alternatives: Avoid separate picker implementations in every lab and edits to vendored lil-gui; retain native selects as the existing value owners.
Keep generation advance and clock reset at their existing separate rebuild points, avoiding a gameplay timing change.
evidence: npm test: 65 test programs passed, including restart/disposal and already-queued callback coverage.
npm run check: syntax, architecture, kernel, assets and presets passed.
npm run test:browser: full source acceptance passed, including keyboard selection, Escape, no-match filtering, dynamic option thresholds, disabled controls, removal and phone-width dialog bounds.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist: full nested-path release acceptance; see artifacts/browser-dist/.

Browser iteration: Enter needed a complete CDP key input including carriage-return text. The subsequent Escape check exposed a close failure with isolated lab key events; an explicit Escape handler fixed it.
Lab JSON import, audio edit, draft preview and normal-game isolation remain verified.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes the extracted ownership and remaining boundaries.
